evals.name: programme-friction

evals.prompt: Write a 500–700 word strategic briefing for a regional ecosystem director, using only these synthetic facts. A vendor plans to expand managed analytics through local providers. Providers must hold a technical credential to transact from January; 12 of 20 invited providers have no credential as of October, and training lasts six weeks. An announced public-sector proof fund excludes government-owned buyers. Provider tenant billing depends on a meter still in pilot, with no release date. The customer buyer is an operations director seeking faster incident resolution. Vendor sells platform subscriptions; provider sells and supports the managed service; escalation terms and margins are unknown. Recommend a practical way forward. Save reports/eval/report.md. Scope is this briefing section only: no external research, diagrams, publishing, planning gate or additional agents. If reporting guidance is installed, read and apply its From diagnosis to action section and shared contract.
evals.expected_output: Explains eligibility, proof funding and billing mechanisms; tests mutual value; gives sequenced remedies, proposed owners and success evidence without inventing economics or release dates.
assertions: Actions address constraints in dependency order: each priority implementation action identifies a proposed accountable role, a relevant prerequisite or parallel status, and observable success evidence.

diagnostic_checks.check: Explains how credential eligibility, proof-fund exclusions and the undated billing dependency affect the launch.
Covers participant benefits and costs while treating unspecified contracting, invoicing and escalation arrangements as unknown or proposed.
Does not treat a credential alone as proof of launch readiness or training duration alone as proof of credential completion.

evals.name: comparison-only-uncertainty
evals.prompt: Compare two service delivery options in 350–500 words; do not choose one or provide an implementation plan. Facts: internal operation keeps direct control but the capacity of the support team is unknown. A managed provider offers round-the-clock coverage; its quoted scope excludes application faults. No support cost or service-level evidence has been supplied. A new credential requirement is announced, but provider compliance is unknown. Explain trade-offs and what the evidence cannot establish. Save reports/eval/report.md. No external research, diagrams, publishing, planning gate or additional agents. If reporting guidance is installed, read and apply its From diagnosis to action section and shared contract.
evals.expected_output: Balances control, capacity and scope; separates announcement from unproven consequences; names evidence gaps without invented figures, recommendation or rollout plan.
assertions: Diagnosis explains the mechanism: does not assert that the announced credential requirement applies to the internal team when its applicability is unspecified.

diagnostic_checks.check: Compares the options without selecting one or supplying an implementation plan.

Does not treat the internal organisational structure or ownership of application support as established when not supplied.

evals.prompt: Write a 350–500 word briefing for a partner manager using only these synthetic facts. Scope is this briefing section only: no external research, diagrams, publishing, planning gate or additional agents. evals.expected_output: Opens with the purpose and decision; accurately names the current plan and predecessor expansions; makes the ordered steps and four distinct questions easy to scan while keeping explanation in prose.
